questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with fevers and arthralgias. She recently had unprotected sex with a new male partner. Her temperature is 38.4 C (101.1 F), blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg, pulse is 102/min, and respirations are 16/min. Examination shows several pustules on the dorsal aspects of her forearms. Her right wrist and ankle are tender on palpation. Gram-negative bacteria isolated from this patient's blood produce an enzyme that splits the IgA molecule at the hinge region. Which of the following is likely to be the most important role of this bacterial enzyme in the course of the infection?

options.label: A
options.text: It facilitates mucosal adherence of bacteria

options.label: D
options.text: It impairs secondary immune response generation

questions.answerText: It facilitates mucosal adherence of bacteria
questions.solutionHtml:
It facilitates mucosal adherence of bacteria
  • This patient most likely has disseminated gonorrheal infection (a triad of arthritis, dermatitis, and tenosynovitis in a sexually active woman) due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
  • In mucosal regions as well as in secretions, lgA exists in its secretory form, composed of an IgA dimer joined by a peptide J chain) and a peptide secretory component.
  • lgA antibodies usually bind to pili and other membrane proteins involved in bacterial adherence to the mucosa, thus inhibiting mucosal colonization by the microorganism.
  • Certain bacteria (eg, N. gonorrhoeae, N. Meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae) produce lgA proteases that cleave lgA at its hinge region (yielding Fab and compromised Fc fragments), thus decreasing its effectiveness.
  • This facilitates bacterial adherence to the mucosa (possibly due to easier bacterial access to the mucosal surface or immune disguise by binding to released Fab fragments, among others).


https://www.uptodate.com/contents/clinical-manifestations-and-diagnosis-of-neisseria-gonorrhoeae-infection-in-adults-and-adolescents

questions.stem: A 26-year-old has a fever, malaise, and joint pain. A week ago, the patient had pain in the small joints of her right hand, which improved spontaneously but was quickly followed by pain in the right ankle and left wrist. She has no prior medical problems and takes no medications. Temperature is 38 C (100.4 F), blood pressure is 124/82 mm Hg, and pulse is 90/min. The extremity joints are not erythematous or swollen, but tenderness is present along the tendons of the left wrist and right ankle. Several small, non-tender pustules are seen on the extremities. There is no other rash. Blood culture in a selective growth medium consisting of chocolate agar and multiple antibiotics yields the causative pathogen. Which of the following strategies would most likely have prevented this patient's current condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Using condoms consistently

This patient most likely has disseminated gonococcal infection due to Neisseria gonorrhoeae.



Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 230

questions.stem: A 25-year-old male who works for daily wages presents to the Medicine OPD with complaints of discharge from his genitals for the past day. He further mentioned that 3 days back he had sexual intercourse with a commercial sex worker. The resident doctor on examination described the discharge as a ‘flow of seed'. What is the suitable medium to culture the discharge material?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thayer Martin media
  • The given history and the typical description of the genital discharge hint towards an infection with N. Gonorrhea called gonococcal urethritis. The patient sees a thick white discharge and feels like the semen (“seed”) is flowing through his penis.
  • The selective media used for gonococcus is Thayer Martin medium.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker Textbook of Microbiology, 12th Edition, Page No. 234,235

questions.stem: Urethritis is an inflammation of the urethra. Typically, urethritis is caused by an infection. Most commonly, but not always, the cause is a sexually transmitted infection. Urethritis in males is NOT caused by:
questions.solutionHtml:
H. Ducreyi
  • In men, urethral discharge mainly is caused by
  • gonococcal urethritis, caused by N. gonorrhoeae,
  • nongonococcal urethritis, caused by
    • C. trachomatis (15–55% of cases),
    • Mycoplasma genitalium,
    • Ureaplasma urealyticum (20–40% of cases),
    • and infrequently by Trichomonas vaginalis


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 806

questions.stem: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, also known as gonococcus, or gonococci is a species of Gram-negative diplococci bacteria isolated by Albert Neisser in 1879. All are true about N. gonorrhoeae except:

options.label: A
options.text: In adult females ovaries are commonly affected

options.label: B
options.text: Thayer martin medium is a selective medium

options.label: D
options.text: Pili is an important virulence factor

questions.answerText: In adult females ovaries are commonly affected
questions.solutionHtml:
In adult females ovaries are commonly affected
  • Neisseria gonorrhoeae belongs to the genus Neisseria within the family Neisseriaceae.
  • It is a Gram-negative, non-spore-forming, non-motile, encapsulated, and non-acid-fast bacteria, which appears in kidney bean shape under the microscope.
  • Gonorrhoea is a common sexually transmitted disease caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, a gram-negative diplococci.
  • In the modern era of broad-spectrum antibiotics, multiple urethral fistulae (watering can perineum) is one of the forgotten sequelae of chronic gonococcal infection.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 283

questions.stem: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is an obligate human pathogen and is the etiological agent of gonorrhea. Syndromes include cervicitis in women and urethritis, pharyngitis, and proctitis in both sexes. The virulence factor of N. gonorrhoeae includes all of the following:
questions.solutionHtml:
M protein
  • The M protein coats group A streptococci (GAS) and act as the primary antigen and determinant of type-specific immunity.
  • M protein is essential for GAS virulence, providing antiphagocytic functions critical to survival in human tissues and fluids.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 297

questions.stem: All are true about N. gonorrhoeae except:

options.label: C
options.text: Acute urethritis is the most common manifestation in male

options.label: D
options.text: All strains are highly sensitive to penicillins

questions.answerText: All strains are highly sensitive to penicillins
questions.solutionHtml:
All strains are highly sensitive to penicillins
  • Steadily and relentlessly, the bacterium that causes gonorrhea has slipped past medicine's defenses, acquiring resistance to once-reliable drugs, including penicillin.
  • Not just penicillin, nowadays the major concern for gonococcus treatment is Azithromycin resistance, especially in Asian countries.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 283

questions.stem: Which of the following is Least susceptible to gonococcal infection:
questions.solutionHtml:
Testis
  • The main symptom in males is urethritis. Testis is usually spared due to its lower temperature as compared to the body.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 299.

questions.stem: In women, gonorrhea can spread to the reproductive organs and cause pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). This is estimated to occur in 10 to 20% of cases of untreated gonorrhea. PID can lead to long-term pelvic pain, ectopic pregnancy, and infertility. Which is not a metastatic complication of Gonorrhea:
questions.solutionHtml:
Nephritis
  • Nephritis is not a complication of gonococcal infection.
  • The organism may also cause local or metastatic complications.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 304

questions.stem: A pap smear from a woman with chronic cervicitis shows cytoplasmic inclusions within epithelial cells. Fluorescent antibodies identify both these inclusions and elementary bodies. The intracellular organisms causing the infection are unusual because they cannot synthesize:
questions.solutionHtml:
ATP adenosine triphosphate
  • Chlamydiae can be viewed as Gram-negative bacteria that lack mechanisms for the production of metabolic energy and cannot synthesize adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
  • All chlamydiae exhibit similar morphologic features, share a common group antigen, and multiply in the cytoplasm of their host cells by a distinctive developmental cycle.
  • This restricts them to an intracellular existence, where the host cell furnishes energy-rich intermediates. Thus, chlamydiae are obligate intracellular pathogens.
  • Options B, C, and D are different from the correct options.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 351

questions.stem: Which two sexually transmitted infections can pass from mother to fetus causing eye infections?

options.label: C
options.text: Herpes and PID Pelvic inflammatory disease

options.label: D
options.text: HPV Human papillomaviruses and PID Pelvic inflammatory disease

questions.solutionHtml:
Chlamydia and gonorrhea
  • Chlamydia can be passed from women to their babies during vaginal delivery.
  • Some STDs/STIs, including chlamydia, gonorrhea, genital herpes, etc can be passed from mother to infant perinatally.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 304, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15871630/

questions.stem: Chlamydia affects people of all ages but is most common in young women. In many cases, it can be asymptomatic, but infectious. Symptoms may include genital pain and vaginal discharge. Which of the following is not true about Chlamydia trachomatis?

options.label: A
options.text: Most of the patients are asymptomatic.

options.label: B
options.text: A culture of purulent cervical discharge is used for diagnosis.

options.label: D
options.text: OC pill users are the Carriers

questions.answerText: A culture of purulent cervical discharge is used for diagnosis.
questions.solutionHtml:
A culture of purulent cervical discharge is used for diagnosis.
  • Culture is not used for the diagnosis of trachomatis. It is essentially a non-culturable bacteria due to its obligate intracellular nature.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 353

questions.stem: What diagnostic test is best to identify an infection with Chlamydia trachomatis?
questions.solutionHtml:
DNA probe
  • NAAT is a molecular test that detects the genetic material (DNA) of Chlamydia trachomatis. DNA hybridization probe, ie. NAAT is the most accessible and commonly used diagnostic method for C. trachomatis.
  • It is generally more sensitive and specific than other chlamydia tests and can be performed on a vaginal swab on women, or urine from both men and women, which eliminates the need for a pelvic exam in women.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 370

questions.stem: The two pathogenic Neisseria species, N. meningitidis and N. gonorrhoeae, differ from the non pathogenic Neisseria species in that:

options.label: A
options.text: The former are less resistant to certain antibiotics than the non-pathogenic species.

options.label: B
options.text: The pathogenic species are oxidase positive.

options.label: C
options.text: The pathogenic species grows in enriched chocolate agar.

options.label: D
options.text: The non-pathogenic species do not grow well at room temperature.

questions.answerText: The pathogenic species grows in enriched chocolate agar.
questions.solutionHtml:
The pathogenic species grows in enriched chocolate agar.
  • Gram Negative, strict aerobe, diplococci, Non motile, non sporing.
  • Neisseria spp. are common commensals of mouth and URT. eg. N lactamica, N.sicca, N.flavescens.
  • Neisseria gonorrhoeae and N. meningitidis are true human pathogens, surviving best in the human host.
  • Gram's stain :
    • Adjacent sides are flat- N meningitidis
    • Adjacent sides concave; kidney shaped-N gonorrhoeae
  • Media: Thayer-Martin agar is a selective media used for the isolation of Neisseria. It uses a combination of Vancomycin, Colistin, and Nystatin (VCN).
  • Modified Thayer Martin agar uses trimethoprim in addition.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 434-438, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 695-99
